traps.p: Facing removal, the Speaker may still speak and vote (2024).

q.stem: With reference to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, consider the following statements: While any resolution for the removal of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha is under consideration
items: He/She shall not have the right to speak.
He/She shall not be entitled to vote on the resolution in the first instance.
q.prompt: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

walk.aarav: Facing removal? No presiding, speaking or voting.
walk.tell: shall not have the right to speak
walk.priya: Article 96: no presiding, but the Speaker may still speak and vote.

items: The Parliament (Prevention of Disqualification) Act, 1959 exempts several posts from disqualification on the grounds of 'Office of Profit'.
The above-mentioned Act was amended five times.
The term 'Office of Profit' is well-defined in the Constitution of India.
q.prompt: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

walk.aarav: The Constitution must define office of profit.
walk.priya: Article 102 uses "office of profit" but never defines it.

q.stem: Which of the following statements is/are correct?
items: A Bill pending in the Lok Sabha lapses on its prorogation.
A Bill pending in the Rajya Sabha, which has not been passed by the Lok Sabha, shall not lapse on dissolution of the Lok Sabha.
q.prompt: Select the correct answer using the code given below.

walk.aarav: Prorogation ends the session. Pending Bills die too.
walk.priya: Article 107(3): prorogation lapses no Bill. Only Lok Sabha dissolution can.
